en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on the Buddha, Concerning the Question on Inference.
7. The Question on Obstacles to Realization “Venerable Nāgasena, suppose here some householder were to commit a *pārājika* offense;
at a later time he might go forth into homelessness, and he himself would not know, ‘I have committed a *pārājika* offense as a householder,’ nor would anyone else [know it of him].”
“Suppose someone were to say to him, ‘You have committed a pārājika offense as a householder.
If he were to act accordingly, would there be a realization of the Dhamma for him?
“Certainly not, Great King.”
“By what cause, venerable sir?
“Because that cause for the realization of the Dhamma has been cut off in him, therefore there is no realization of the Dhamma.
“Venerable Nāgasena, you say:”
“When one knows, there is remorse; when there is remorse, there is an obstruction; when the mind is obstructed, there is no realization of the Dhamma.

But for one who does not know, who is free from remorse, and who dwells with a peaceful mind—for what reason would there be no realization of the Dhamma? This question proceeds by way of an uneven comparison; reflect upon it and then answer.
“Does a seed that is well-prepared, well-planted, and well-sown grow in a field that is well-tilled and well-manured, O Great King?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“But would that very same seed, O Great King, grow upon the surface of a solid rock?
“No, venerable sir.”
“But why, Great King, does that very same seed grow in the mud, and why does it not grow on a solid rock?
“Venerable sir, there is no cause for that seed to grow on a solid rock; without a cause, the seed does not grow.

“In the same way, Great King, whatever cause there might have been for the realization of the Dhamma, that cause has been cut off for him; without a cause, the realization of the Dhamma does not occur.”
"Or again, Great King, just as sticks, clods of earth, balls, and clubs find their place upon the earth—would those very same sticks, clods, balls, and clubs, Great King, find their place in the sky?
"No indeed, venerable sir.
"What then, Great King, is the reason why those very same sticks, clods, balls, and clubs find their place upon the earth, but do not remain in the sky?"
“There is no cause, venerable sir, for those sticks, clods of earth, lumps of clay, and clubs to remain suspended in the air; they do not remain there without a cause.
“In the same way, great king, his realization has been cut off by that very fault. When the cause is uprooted, there is no realization without a cause.
Or again, great king, suppose a fire burns on dry land: would that same fire burn in water?”
“No indeed, Bhante.
“But what is the reason here, Great King, by which that very same fire burns on dry land, and for what reason it does not burn in water?
“There is no cause, Bhante, in water for the burning of fire; lacking a cause, it does not burn.”
“In the same way, Great King, for him the cause for the realization [of the Dhamma] has been cut off by that hatred; when the cause is uprooted, there is no realization of the Dhamma without a cause.

“Venerable Nāgasena, consider this matter further. My mind is not convinced of it. How can there be an obstruction for one who does not know, who is without mindfulness, and without remorse? Convince me with a reason.
“But tell me, Great King, if someone eats the *halāhala* poison without knowing it is poison, does it take away his life?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, even an evil deed committed by one who is unaware becomes an obstacle to spiritual realization.
Would fire, great king, burn one who steps upon it unknowingly?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, even an evil deed committed by one who is unaware acts as an obstacle to spiritual realization.
Would a venomous snake, having bitten someone who is unaware, take away their life, great king?”
“Yes, venerable sir.
“In the same way, great king, even an evil deed committed by one who is ignorant acts as an obstacle to spiritual realization.
Did you not hear, great king, how the King of Kalinga, the son of Kolankara, though surrounded by the seven treasures, mounted the elephant-treasure—”
“Even while going to visit his family, though he was unaware, he was unable to pass above the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
This, O Great King, is the reason why even an evil deed committed unknowingly becomes an obstacle to full realization.
“The word of the Conqueror, venerable Nāgasena, cannot be contradicted; this is its meaning, and I accept it as such.”
The seventh question: on that which creates an obstacle to clear realization.
